claims.text: The starting material is a W–Cu composite with W particles or interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
The proposed intervention is incorporation of 0.1–0.5 wt% Ag into the Cu phase before consolidation and sintering.
Ag addition creates an Ag-enriched interfacial layer between W and Cu during sintering.
The Ag-enriched W–Cu interfacial layer is coherent.
Trace Ag promotes transient liquid-phase sintering in the proposed W–Cu processing regime.
Ag lowers the interfacial energy between W and Cu.
Ag improves interfacial bonding between W and Cu.
The Ag-modified interface mitigates phase separation.
The Ag-modified interface suppresses interfacial void formation.
The Ag-modified interface remains more stable and defect-free under subsequent heat-transfer and irradiation conditions than the untreated interface.
The improved interface transmits heat more effectively than the untreated W–Cu interface.
The Ag-doped composite will have higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise identically processed Ag-free W–Cu composite.
Untreated W–Cu composites are expected to exhibit phase separation and interfacial voids under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
The proposed effect is expected to apply to vacuum or inert-atmosphere processing at temperatures up to approximately 1100°C.
The proposed effect is expected to persist under combined thermal and irradiation service conditions relevant to W-based plasma-facing material/Cu-based cooling-component joints.
